newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Samsung Elec shrs unmoved by S&P rating news. [CORRECTED 04:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Samsung Elec shrs unmoved by S&P rating news. [CORRECTED 04:10 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects headline to read "rating news" rather than "rating cut" and corrects text to make clear that Samsung's rating outlook was negative)
Share prices of South Korean chipmaker Samsung Electronics Co were unmoved by news that Standard & Poor's Corp had cut Samsung's long-term rating outlook to negative from stable, brokers said.
By late morning on Thursday, Samsung shares were trading at 60,000 won, up 400 won on the day.

Standard & Poor's said on Thursday the rating outlook cut was based on concerns that a protracted downturn in the semiconductor industry would cause Samsung to rely more on debt to finance its rapid growth both at home and abroad.
"The news was shrugged off because investors thought the company's share prices have already reflected major negative factors," said Kim Ik-hwan of Hyundai Securities.
